gap: No result ChatGPT got states the inverter's own no-load draw. Over 72 hours that draw is about as large as the freezer's own use or larger: The Solar Lab measured the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus at about 58 W idle (about 4.2 kWh over 72 h), and Zelpio measured the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus at about 112 W (about 8.1 kWh over 72 h, enough to empty its 3,840 Wh in about 34 h). Both figures are bigger than the 3 kWh that ChatGPT's 'typical' freezer uses in 3 days.
standout_why: I compared the cited pages us.ecoflow.com DELTA Pro 3 (it returned HTTP 429 and could not be read) and ankersolix.com/products/f3800 (it shows no idle or self-consumption figure), plus the top result solarwaypoint.com's three-way comparison. Solarwaypoint lists capacity, output, solar ports, cycles and UPS time, but says outright that idle and efficiency are 'not listed' for all three. ChatGPT's answer divides nameplate Wh by 1 kWh/day at a flat 85% and gets 4.3 days for the 5000 Plus and 3.3 for the F3800 Plus, so it never counts the inverter's standing draw. None of these pages gives a percentage with its cycle-life figure either.
decides: This reverses ChatGPT's ranking. If you add the measured idle draw to a 1 kWh/day freezer, the Jackery 5000 Plus drops from 4.3 days to about 2.1 days (5,040 ÷ (1,000 + 58×24 = 2,392 Wh/day)). The F3800 Plus drops from 3.3 days to about 1.0 day at Zelpio's 112 W (3,840 ÷ 3,688), or about 1.6 days if Anker's update halving idle draw has been installed. The Solar Lab measured the original F3800 at only about 10 W idle (about 240 Wh/day), which gives about 3.1 days on the same sums. So whichever station draws least at idle wins, not the one with the biggest battery. The page should tell buyers to check the measured idle watts, keep the firmware current (the F3800 Plus fix is only in the June 2025 update), and use solar to cover the idle draw as well as the freezer: with idle at 58 W or more, the 400 W array that ChatGPT says 'offsets the freezer' covers only about half of the real daily draw. I found no sourced idle figure for the DELTA Pro 3, so it can't be ranked on this measure yet.

findings.label: Measured idle draw, inverter on, no load
findings.value: about 58 W (about 1.39 kWh/day; about 4.18 kWh over 72 h)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Real Competition for the Anker F3800 and DELTA Pro Ultra? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'sitting around 58W per hour when we turned the inverter on and let it run through a full charge without any sort of load'. The review gives no date or author. Method: 58 W × 24 = 1,392 Wh/day and × 72 = 4,176 Wh. 5,040 ÷ (1,000 + 1,392) = 2.1 days with a 1 kWh/day freezer. Idle draw partly overlaps with conversion loss once a load is running, so this runtime is a conservative estimate.

findings.label: Measured surge vs claimed
findings.value: Failed to start a 10,000 W surge air conditioner. Ran 8,000 W and 9,500 W loads for 20–30 s. Jackery claims 14,000 W.
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Surge has no bearing on a freezer's compressor start (a few hundred W). I include it only to show the gap between claimed and measured surge.

findings.label: Measured idle draw, inverter on, nothing plugged in
findings.value: about 112 W (1,350 Wh in 12 h; about 2.7 kWh/day; about 8.1 kWh over 72 h)
findings.note: Zelpio, published 2026-08-23. The review does not state the firmware version. Zelpio also measured AC capacity at 83% of the rated 3,840 Wh and blames the idle draw for part of that. Method: 3,840 ÷ (1,000 + 2,688) = 1.04 days with a 1 kWh/day freezer, and the unit with no load empties in about 34 h.

findings.label: Idle draw on stock firmware vs after Anker's update
findings.value: Anker says the update cuts idle consumption by 50% and doubles standby time. It gives no figures in watts. The post covers the F3800 Plus only.
findings.source_title: Increase Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Standby Time to the Max with the Latest Firmware Update (Anker SOLIX)
findings.note: Post dated June 27, 2025. It gives no firmware version number or test conditions. If the 50% applies to Zelpio's 112 W, idle would be about 56 W, or 1.34 kWh/day: 3,840 ÷ 2,344 = 1.6 days at 1 kWh/day. This is the clearest stock-firmware vs updated-firmware case on the shortlist.

findings.label: Measured efficiency at high load
findings.value: 84% (6,000 W inverter pushed from a full battery)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus (The Solar Lab results page)
findings.note: The test was at high load, not at a freezer's level. The page also reports that the unit accepted the full 3,200 W of solar. The page gives no idle number, although it says idle was tested.

findings.label: Measured idle draw (original F3800, in a 24-hour outage test)
findings.source_title: Can You Survive a 24-Hour Outage with a Power Station? - Backup Power with the Anker F3800 (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'the main unit consumed around 10 watts per hour just to keep its internal systems running'. In the same test a refrigerator drew a steady 30 W (720 Wh/day) and spiked briefly to 400 W at start. Method: 3,840 ÷ (1,000 + 240) = 3.1 days at 1 kWh/day. This conflicts with the How-To Geek claim of 'over 1 kWh in 24 h', which I could not open (see unsourced).

findings.label: Measured efficiency and solar input
findings.value: 89% at a 3,650 W load. Solar 'Hit 2,600W Easily'. Surge held at 5,100 W for nearly a minute.
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (The Solar Lab results page)
findings.note: The page says idle draw was tested but prints no number. The efficiency was measured at high load, so it says nothing about the overhead at a freezer's 50–150 W.

findings.label: Solar input ratings normalised to the voltage window each port accepts
findings.source_title: Anker Solix F3800 vs EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 vs Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Comparison - Solar Waypoint
findings.note: The 5000 Plus's 4,000 W figure applies only to strings of 135 V or more. A 400–800 W set of portable panels for a freezer would usually land on the 1,200 W low-voltage port, so the headline solar number doesn't matter for this question. Solarwaypoint lists no idle, efficiency or price for any of the three.

findings.label: Solar input as now shown on Anker's /products/f3800 page
findings.value: 2 ports × 1,600 W, 11–165 V, 17 A (3,200 W). Output 2,400 W from the 120 V outlets, 6,000 W total. UPS 20 ms. 3,000+ cycles with no % given. 5-year warranty. Listed as Sold Out with no price shown.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Portable Power Station - 3840Wh | 6000W - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: This URL is the one ChatGPT cited. It now shows specs that match the F3800 Plus (3,200 W at 11–165 V), not the original F3800's 2 × 1,200 W at 11–60 V as listed by Solarwaypoint. The page has no idle or self-consumption figure.

unsourced: DELTA Pro 3 measured idle draw. A search snippet put The Solar Lab's figure at 37 W, but the results page I opened prints no idle number, and the full review has none. EcoFlow's manual PDFs could not be fetched as text (one is over 10 MB, the others are binary), and manuals.ecoflow.com returned an empty shell.
How-To Geek's 'F3800 uses over 1 kWh in 24 h with nothing plugged in'. The only copy is syndicated on Yahoo, which returned 403, so I could not open it.
A maker's own idle or no-load watt figure for any of the four. The Anker product page and Jackery FAQ list none. The Jackery product page returned 429.

Cycle life tied to a capacity % (80% vs 70%) for the DELTA Pro 3 (4,000), F3800 (3,000) and 5000 Plus (3,000). Neither the maker pages I could open nor Solarwaypoint state the %, and the manuals could not be read.
